findings.where: Style tile, the motion sketch's principle words "calm, smooth, precise" (desktop and phone); also the lecture title link "Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the ‘Abundance’ Challenge" in the article specimen
findings.fault: The tile's own type pair says Gelasio is for headings and reading, and Source Sans is for "the nav, buttons, labels and dates only". Yet the principle words are a display-size heading set in Source Sans SemiBold, in the paler second-text grey that no other heading uses. The lecture's title, which is the name of a piece of Mark's writing, is also set in Source Sans, while the article title above it is in Gelasio. So the tile breaks the rule it sets.
findings.who_objects: The layout and animation rounds that inherit this tile, and Angélique adding posts and PDFs. They get two answers to which face a heading or a title takes, and the site's headings will drift between a serif and a sans.

findings.where: Style tile, the section labels "Palette", "Texture", "Type pair", "An article page" and "Motion sketch" (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: These five labels are the same kind of part, but they are treated differently. "Texture" and "Motion sketch" have a full-width hairline rule under them. "Palette", "Type pair" and "An article page" have none. On desktop this puts a rule under one column's label and not the other's on the same row.
findings.who_objects: A designer in the layout round reading the tile as the house standard for section headings. They can't tell whether a section label takes a rule, so the pattern will be applied unevenly across the site.

findings.where: Hero supporting line "World Bank's PPP Group" (desktop and phone first screen); article specimen title "The World's Best…"; the Gelasio caption "Georgia's proportions… the logo's"
findings.fault: Apostrophes are straight typewriter marks, and in Gelasio at hero size the mark shows as a vertical tick. The same page sets its quotation marks curly (“ ” and ‘Abundance’). Curly quotes beside straight apostrophes look like text pasted in unchecked, and the first one is on the first screen.
findings.who_objects: Mark, a lawyer whose work is careful wording, and an agency reader used to edited documents. They would see the mismatch as a lack of finish. Angélique will copy the specimen's typography into new posts.
